design_note: The earlier labs teach sample-size bounds and judge false acceptance. This evidence map adds order sensitivity in pairwise grading. A switched winner flags instability while the sparse stochastic evidence prevents the stronger causal claim that position alone explains the change.

source.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
source.concept: LLM judges can exhibit position bias when comparing responses. Judge agreement should be assessed with attention to evaluation design and known sources of bias.
source.scope: Reply R, reply S and both verdicts are fictional. Two observations illustrate an order-consistency check, not an estimated bias rate or a reproduced experimental result.

lesson.anchor: Paired comparisons, slices and failure taxonomies
lesson.title: Swap the display order before trusting the winner
lesson.intro: A ShopAssist judge compares fixed replies R and S under one rubric. In one constructed trial R appears first; in the other S appears first. Each trial uses a fresh stochastic judgment.

claims.text: The same reply won both presentations.
The first displayed reply won in both trials.
Display position alone caused the winner to change.

sources.text: Pair audit: R won the R/S presentation; S won the S/R presentation.
Verdict log: the first slot was selected in both presentations.
Only one stochastic judgment was collected for each display order.

data.verdict: Order consistency failed; neither a sole cause nor a best reply is established.

read: Map verdicts back to reply identities, not only first or second labels.
The visible pair is inconsistent about which content is better.
One stochastic trial per order cannot isolate position as the only cause.
lesson.question: Can the original R-first verdict alone establish that R is the better reply?
lesson.answer: No. The swapped presentation chooses S, so this pair provides no stable winner. Use balanced orders, repeated or appropriately controlled judgments, and rubric-based adjudication. The two rows flag an evaluation weakness without proving a population bias rate or which reply is actually better.
lesson.takeaway: Test judge consistency under harmless presentation changes.
lesson.assumption: Constructed pair; reply content and rubric stay fixed. Stochastic judgment remains uncontrolled, and neither reply's true quality is established.
lesson.source_label: Zheng et al.: LLM judge position bias
